risk_note: RV2 by PR (platform/events and platform/queue; notification RV1). notification consumes risk.state_changed (EVENT_SUBSCRIPTIONS entry, evt.notification-risk-state queue, worker concurrency 5, wired on the worker entry only and built lazily) and writes the BR-TEXT-23 RISK_STATE_CHANGED inbox message: frozen / frozen_until / unfrozen / banned / unbanned; moves through appealing and moves with no variant (normal to normal) send nothing. Body defaults are BR-TEXT-23 verbatim, reason_category from the category table, frozen_until from the event payload snapshot (B1-03y) formatted per BR-TEXT-11 against the injected Clock in +08:00 (same year MM-DD HH:mm, other years YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm); notify_templates overrides by variant. notify_logs (dedupe_key risk.state_changed:<event_id>) and inbox_messages are written in one transaction; a redelivered or concurrent event leaves one message and one log. Inbox only, no push or SMS; user_risk_state is not read. unbanned carries {need_reauth} (购物前需重新完成淘宝授权。) only when the user's taobao union_binding is invalid when the message is generated (BR-TEXT-23 as clarified in SPEC_REF fde86795d3a2), read through a linking read-only port. createHttpApp now starts the real JOB_QUEUE by default when database handles are given (onApplicationBootstrap of a wrapping root module, the last step of init; startQueue: false opts out) and stops it through the platform shutdown hook (HTTP, then queue, then database), so api-entry integration tests enqueue in the same transaction as production does (orchestrator ruling C); entry.ts passes startQueue: false and keeps its own start before listen, so the production start and shutdown order are unchanged. Root cause of the earlier failures: replacing app.init / app.close with Object.assign was silently dropped by Nest's application Proxy. The two platform wiring unit tests opt out with startQueue: false; the frozen min-version assembly test opted out through the separate test-change B1-12i (#906, orchestrator ruling ②); no assertion changes. The two platform contract tests add only this subscription, queue and worker (ledger test_paths; class 1, label under approvals #24); no assertion changes. The earlier kit-level startQueue: true change (ruling A, B1-12h) was dropped when rebasing on 10-21: ruling C starts the queue by default, so no kit needs it.
